title: Trace and base-change rearrangement before the first triangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. Schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ for the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring, $D(Z)=D(\Mod_{R_Z})$ for its unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $\mathcal L(Z)=\Loc(\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E))$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible, sk-def-localizing-closure]. Pullbacks and direct images are the canonical derived functors with adjunction $h^*\dashv Rh_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], and pullback coefficients are identified by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. All tensors are derived tensors over $R_Z$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a proper $h:Z\to B$, let $\pi_{h,L,N}:L\otimes Rh_*N\to Rh_*(h^*L\otimes N)$ be the canonical projection map, the adjoint transpose of $1\otimes c_{h,N}$, where $c_h$ is the canonical counit.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper, let $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and use the canonical identification $fp_1=fp_2$. Put $T_Y=R_Y(1)[2]$, $T_X=f^*T_Y$, and $T_W=p_1^*T_X=p_2^*T_X$, with twists as in [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] and pullback/tensor comparisons as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $b_2:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ and $b_1:f^*Rf_*\to Rp_{1*}p_2^*$ be the canonical base-change mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Assume these and the projection maps used below are isomorphisms on $\mathcal L$ and that the displayed functors preserve $\mathcal L$. Take morphisms $t:Rf_*T_X\to R_Y$ and $t_i:Rp_{i*}T_W\to R_X$ satisfying $t_i\circ b_{i,T_X}=f^*t$ for $i=1,2$. Define $G(K)=f^*K\otimes T_X$ and
$$e_K=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\pi_{f,K,T_X}^{-1}:Rf_*GK\to K.$$
For $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ define the natural isomorphism
$$B_N:Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)\xrightarrow{\pi_{p_2,T_X,p_1^*N}^{-1}}Rp_{2*}p_1^*N\otimes T_X\xrightarrow{b_{2,N}^{-1}\otimes1}GRf_*N,$$
where the first arrow uses the canonical tensor symmetries.

For every $N\in\mathcal L(X)$ one has
$$e_{Rf_*N}\circ Rf_*(B_N)=Rf_*(1_N\otimes t_1)\circ Rf_*(\pi_{p_1,N,T_W}^{-1}).$$
The source of the left side is $Rf_*Rp_{2*}(p_1^*N\otimes T_W)$; that of the right side is identified with it by $Rf_*Rp_{2*}\simeq R(fp_2)_*=R(fp_1)_*\simeq Rf_*Rp_{1*}$. Both targets are $Rf_*N$.

Descend ordinary braiding compatibility on flat resolutions; use the existing generic derived-braiding wrapper, whose braiding field is definitionally the specified Koszul construction. Prove monoidality of ordinary pullback composition by the conjugate pushforward tensor identity, checked after the balanced-tensor quotient. Derivation preserves that tensor identity by leftDerivedTensorComparison_naturality_app and map_leftDerivedTensorComparison_app_app_comp. These caches are definitionally the existing constructions. TraceFirstAssertion uses the same TraceFirstFormula through traceDataFormula and the fields of traceNativeComparisonData. The bundle changes no map; it avoids proof-abstraction comparisons between independently expanded monoidal instances. Prove the bundled trace assembly over fully abstract ordinary abelian categories before any specialization to internal modules, and construct the proof-only derived braided functor instances inside that proof. The native square proof refers directly to the canonical leftDerivedTensorComparison; its unused public native alias is removed. Reassociate the square-family equation with Category.assoc explicitly; transport the canonical unit equality using the proved generic equality-transport helper. Express tensor compatibility as the private predicate traceDataSquare over the same canonical comparison-data bundle. Prove the entire composition-family square calculation over abstract ordinary abelian categories, and only then specialize this folded proposition to the native sheaf-module pullbacks.

proof.text: Perform the Kunneth factorization directly for the three monoidal categories in the statement. Transpose the two composites through the composite adjunctions; mate-counit equations and the tensor compatibility of the specified square make their transposes equal. The conjugate square identifies their targets. The symmetric projection maps in direct-image-first and fixed-input-first order are identified by their adjunction transposes. Expanding B gives its inverse as the second factorization after the base-change map. This is the same argument as the ringed Kunneth lemma, with no conversion to a different ringed-topos model.

proof.text: Prove naturality of B by naturality of projection, square mate and the two braidings. For the trace equation cancel the invertible projection and B, substitute the first Kunneth factorization, and move the square component through projection by naturality. Cancel the first inverse projection. Combine the scalar factors and apply trace1. The left-coefficient projection action, its naturality and right unit normalization identify the result with tensoring by the trace followed by the right unitor. Specialize this general calculation to the canonical condensed-module derived operations. The specialization compares applications of the same comparison-data bundle, keeping the concrete derived monoidal structures out of declared types.
